basis: HPV produces anogenital skin lesions; perianal location does not establish anal mucosal disease as defining or present in >=30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: perianal skin is dermatologic; anal canal involvement is neither required nor established in >=30% across this concept.

basis: FRAXD is a chromosomal fragile-site designation; no established organ phenotype is supplied. Intellectual disability cannot be inferred from the fragile-site name or gene.

decisions.neurologic: none: the record gives no intellectual disability, neurologic definition or neurologic ancestry; FRAXD alone does not establish brain disease.

basis: Hyperparathyroid metabolic bone disease defined by bone resorption, fibrous replacement, cysts and fractures.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: osteitis fibrosa is a metabolic bone disorder defined by excessive parathyroid hormone action, rather than an unrelated endocrine association.

basis: Defining renal, adrenal and lung dysgenesis; oral clefts 2/3 and bowel malrotation 30-79%. Cardiac defects 30-79% omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted under the cap; oral clefts have a specific 2/3 estimate plus frequent bowel malrotation.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate/lip in 2/3 and bowel malrotation in 30-79% establish common structural gastrointestinal involvement.

basis: A vascular neoplasm arising in the brain; both brain location and blood-vessel origin define the lesion.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangioma is a neoplasm of blood vessels, which belong to this axis; systemic vascular disease is not required.

basis: Bone dysplasia; neuronal migration defects and lung hypoplasia each 80-99%. Urinary abnormality is unspecified; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish damage.

decisions.renal: none: urinary abnormality is reported in 80-99%, but no specific malformation or functional impairment establishes direct urinary-organ damage.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; visual impairment ~50-75%, cardiac and renal/urinary malformations each ~25-50%. Joint laxity alone does not establish damaging skeletal disease.

decisions.renal: involved: congenital renal/urinary malformations occur in approximately 25-50%; the usual range supports inclusion near the 30% threshold.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent visual impairment occurs in approximately 50-75%, commonly from refractive and ocular alignment abnormalities.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint laxity and minor skeletal traits are common, but damaging locomotor abnormalities are not established in >=30%.

basis: Intracranial arterial-wall disease; subarachnoid hemorrhage in 7/17 (~41%) is a separately diagnosed rupture complication.

decisions.neurologic: none: subarachnoid hemorrhage affects 7/17 (~41%), but is a separately diagnosed complication; intracranial arterial location alone is cardiovascular.

basis: Brain, lung and liver disease define the syndrome; anemia in 7/7 supports blood involvement. Thin bone cortices and delayed skeletal maturation, each 7/7, omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia in 7/7 demonstrates common blood dysfunction and is retained as the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: thin bone cortices and delayed skeletal maturation each occur in 7/7; omitted under the cap in favor of established blood dysfunction.

basis: Glycosylation defect with encephalopathy; coagulopathy and scoliosis 30-79%. Ocular findings omitted at cap; enteropathy and renal/hepatic dysfunction 5-29%.

decisions.haematologic: involved: coagulopathy is an additional systemic manifestation, with blood abnormalities in 30-79%; the defining disorder is glycosylation-related encephalopathy.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea occurs in 30-79%, but proven protein-losing enteropathy is 5-29%; symptoms alone do not establish intestinal damage.
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus/ocular abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but are omitted under the cap in favor of coagulopathy and structural scoliosis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural scoliosis and skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%, meeting the threshold for direct locomotor involvement.
